oracle.answer: Article 198 of the Egypt's Civil Code establishes rules regarding interest rates when there is a delay in paying money owed. It says that both sides can agree on an extra fee (interest), but they cannot charge more than 7%. If they decide on a higher percentage, then the highest allowed amount (7%) applies, and anything over that must be returned. Also, fees or charges added to loans have strict limits; if these go beyond what’s allowed, they might be seen as hidden interest and could be adjusted down unless proven otherwise.
